newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Economists say Sfr may be near undervalued levels.
newsitem.headline: Economists say Sfr may be near undervalued levels.

text.p: A group of independent Swiss economists said in a report compiled in January that it was possible the Swiss franc was near levels where it could be considered undervalued.
They also said a rise in the franc, despite any undervaluation, would be negative for the economy, and said they expected the current situation to persist.
The report, entitled "A Manifesto by Swiss Economists" and issued by Institut 'Crea' at the University of Lausanne, said the weak Swiss economy had been helped by the franc's declines.
The group of 23 economists, mostly based at Swiss universities, noted that the franc, which had started to weaken, briefly appreciated in July and August.

"Since then, the depreciating trend has thankfully re-asserted itself, and rather powerfully at that, to such an extent that the franc may now be somewhat undervalued vis-a-vis at least the mark, although perhaps not (yet?) vis-a-vis the US dollar," the report said.

In a footnote, the group added that according to some Crea calculations, "for what they are worth," the fundamental market equilibrium exchange rates were of the order of 80.00 Swiss centimes to the mark, and 1.40 francs to the dollar as of September 1996.
On Wednesday afternoon the Swiss currency was trading at about 1.4280 francs to the dollar, and 86.65 centimes to the mark.
The report added that "things could go wrong" again, leading the franc to appreciate. One worry was a possible strengthening due to turmoil in introducing European Monetary and Economic Union (EMU).

"In that respect, one often-mentioned danger is that the EMU process is still far from completed and that all sorts of problems might still arise on the road to a common European currency, which -- should they happen -- might very well put the franc under upward pressure again," the report said.
The report also said the franc's levels could translate into upward price pressure.
"Insofar as the franc is headed for a longish period of undervaluation, this is likely to put some upward pressures on the general price level," the study said.
The group of economists included a vice-director at a study centre of the Swiss National Bank in Gerzensee.
A spokesman for the SNB said the study centre provides training in central banking, especially for bankers from emerging countries, and also has its own body of economists.
He said the research done at the centre was independent of that used by the SNB to make policy decisions.
